uncertain: UART selection pads were treated as configuration jumpers (like DIP switches), not wiring points; if they should count, they form a 2x4 pad block labeled TX G18/G7/G14/G10 and RX G17/G13/G6/G0 (top to bottom).
notes: Back view of the M5 Module LLM (AX630C) with a function block overlay. The 2x15 M-Bus header on the right has no pin labels in the image (only stray silkscreen fragments such as 5V/DSU partly hidden by the overlay). The labeled 'UART' block is a 2x4 set of selection jumper pads (TX: G18/G7/G14/G10, RX: G17/G13/G6/G0) with a table mapping them to CoreS3/Core2/Core pins (default G18/G17 on CoreS3, G13/G14 on Core2, G16/G17 on Core); it selects which bus pins carry UART rather than providing wiring points. No labeled physical pin positions, so no connector map.
